review.assessment: Scope Check: The task requires fixing billing logic so that printed per-line amounts sum exactly to the displayed invoice total. This diff only introduces `billing/pricing.py` and shows no changes to receipt formatting or summation orchestration in other files. Without seeing how lines are rendered versus aggregated downstream, I must evaluate this change entirely on its own arithmetic design. The module explicitly uses IEEE 754 floats for all monetary calculations and defers rounding until the very end of summation (`money.quantize(running)`). This design directly contradicts financial accuracy requirements and will not satisfy the task's consistency constraint.

findings.actual: `total_of` accumulates unrounded `line.total` values as floats and calls `money.quantize` only once after the loop. If receipts print rounded per-line amounts (standard for invoices), their printed sum will diverge from this final quantized total.
findings.defect: Why delayed rounding breaks line-to-total consistency
findings.expected: Each line's monetary contribution should be quantized (rounded to 2 decimal places) before being added to the running total, ensuring printed lines and invoice totals match exactly.

findings.actual: The module relies on `float` for all intermediate computations (`subtotal`, `discount`, `net`, `tax`) and final amounts. Binary floating-point representation introduces inherent precision errors that compound during addition.
findings.defect: Why float arithmetic is unsuitable for currency in this module
findings.expected: Monetary values must be handled with exact decimal representation (`decimal.Decimal` or integer-based cents) from the point of entry, eliminating binary rounding drift.
